_comment: Assertions for the Horizontal Non-Web Capacity Guard + the eco/basic sizing-table rows it depends on. A persistent non-web formation with quantity > 1 is routed off Elastic Beanstalk onto Fargate (design-mapping.md 'Horizontal Non-Web Capacity Guard'), so the Fargate table must carry every dyno tier the EB table carries — otherwise the lookup misses and the formation is dropped from the design with only a warning.
guard_rule_from_inventory: process_type != 'web' AND quantity > 1 MUST map to Fargate

sizing_tables._comment: Cross-table regression guard: the guard can move a formation from the EB table to the Fargate table, and the EKS branch reuses the same tier names, so the three tables must agree on the tier set.

fargate_cpu_memory_matrix._source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html — 'Task CPU and memory' (verified 2026-08-01). Fargate rejects any other pairing at RunTask time.

fargate_matrix_baseline._comment: PRE-EXISTING violations, not introduced by this fixture: 8192 CPU units cap at 61440 MiB (60 GB), but these rows request 65536 MiB (64 GB). Fixing them is a sizing decision (drop to 60 GB or move up to 16384 CPU) tracked separately. Every other row — and every new row — is checked against the matrix.
